topic: How can satellite link budgets be optimized for high throughput and low latency in global aeronautical coverage?
consensus_response: To optimize satellite link budgets for high throughput and low latency in global aeronautical coverage, it is essential to address the high fixed latency and varying link conditions. This can be achieved by implementing adaptive modulation and coding techniques to adjust the data rate based on the available capacity, reducing transmission time and improving throughput. Additionally, leveraging advanced queuing strategies, such as priority queuing, can help manage data transmission and minimize latency. Furthermore, the use of Li-Fi Over Satellite (LOS) technology and Optical Inter-Satellite Links (OISLs) can provide high-speed, low-latency connections between satellites, reducing dependence on ground stations and enabling more efficient data transmission. The increasing use of Software-Defined Satellites (SDS) can also enable dynamic reconfiguration of satellite resources, improving resource allocation and QoS.
reference_context: Satellite links have high fixed latency due to signal propagation time, and varying link conditions can impact throughput. Ku-band frequencies offer higher throughput but increased latency. Advanced modulation techniques, such as Adaptive Modulation and Coding (AMC), can improve throughput and reduce latency. Li-Fi Over Satellite (LOS) technology and Optical Inter-Satellite Links (OISLs) can provide high-speed, low-latency connections between satellites. Software-Defined Satellites (SDS) can enable dynamic reconfiguration of satellite resources, improving resource allocation and QoS.
